title: The mythical creature running your household
dek: Not a lore exam. Twelve questions about who keeps this place standing, what goes missing, and which saucer nobody admits to leaving out.

questions.prompt: The house is suspiciously tidy and one thing is missing. You assume:

options.label: I fixed it in my sleep and forgot
Something has been through my drawers
This is the calm before something loud
The house is in a mood again

questions.prompt: A visitor says the place has a lovely atmosphere. You hear:
questions.helper: Pick the thought that arrives first.

options.label: They noticed the one thing I obsess over
They are casing the place
Wait until they hear the pipes
I will pretend I did not hear that

questions.prompt: A warning about the house should arrive as:

options.label: A note left where I'll find it
A joke that lands badly

questions.prompt: One object explains this household. Which one is on the shelf?

options.label: A glass of milk, left out
A broom nobody owns
options.alt: A worn broom leaning against a door

options.label: One very good spoon
A coat that smells of the sea
options.alt: A heavy coat hanging by a doorway

questions.helper: Across: does it get tidied or disturbed. Up: does it stay or hoard.

questions.prompt: Rank what this household needs most tonight.
questions.helper: First place is the thing you'd deal with first.

items.label: Everything put back where it was

questions.helper: One phrase per gap. The house is listening.
questions.template: This house only works because {a}, and nobody mentions {b}.

options.label: someone is awake at 2am fixing it
things go missing and come back changed
there's a hoard behind a door
the good room stays closed
the noise in the pipes
the thing at the bottom of the garden
who actually pays for it
how often everyone leaves

questions.prompt: I can tell a room is about to go wrong.
I'd rather things were left exactly as they are.
If something of mine goes missing, I take it personally.

options.label: Fix it before anyone wakes up
Leave it and blame the house
Announce it, dramatically
Add it to the list for later

questions.prompt: The last thing a visitor notices on the way out:

options.label: How clean it all is
That something is missing
The noise from upstairs
That they'd like to stay

results.name: The Brownie
results.tagline: Tidies at 2am, expects one saucer of milk
results.blurb: You are the reason the house works and the reason nobody knows why. You fix things quietly, at inconvenient hours, and keep a very precise mental list of what everyone owes you in acknowledgement. It is a long list.
strengths: Notices the small thing before it becomes a big thing
Keeps a household running on goodwill and lists
results.watchOut: Being indispensable is not the same as being thanked. Ask, once, out loud.

results.name: The Bogart
results.blurb: You are the reason the house has a memory and a sense of humour about it. Nothing is ever quite where it was, and somehow that is how you know everything is fine. You keep the things people aren't ready to look at yet.
strengths: Finds what everyone else has given up on
Keeps a secret like a locked cupboard
Makes a house feel inhabited rather than staged
results.watchOut: Not every missing thing is a joke. Say when you've taken something.

results.name: The Banshee
results.tagline: Announces the problem before it happens
results.blurb: You can hear a household going wrong from three rooms away, and you would rather say it now than be polite about it later. People call it dramatic right up until you're correct. Then they call it something else.
strengths: Catches problems early and says so
Doesn't let a small thing rot quietly
Surprisingly good in an actual emergency
results.watchOut: A warning every day stops sounding like a warning. Save the wail.

results.name: The Kelpie
results.tagline: Offers a lovely ride. Do not accept.
results.blurb: Your household runs on momentum and a little danger. You are charming, unpredictable, and the reason there is always a story about the boiler. You don't mean any harm. You do mean to see what happens.
strengths: Turns a dull Tuesday into something worth retelling
Fearless about trying the wrong way first
Gets other people out of their routines
results.watchOut: Other people have to live here too. Give them a heads-up.

results.name: The Dragon
results.blurb: You keep the house stocked, warm and slightly over-full. There is a drawer with batteries, a shelf with every charger, and a cupboard nobody else is allowed to reorganise. Your care looks like inventory, and it is enormously effective.
results.watchOut: A hoard is not a personality. Let some of it go.

results.name: The Selkie
results.tagline: Leaves the coat by the door
results.blurb: You come and go, and the house is better for both. You arrive with your whole attention, then disappear for a while and return with stories. The people who love you have learned not to chase the coat.
strengths: Brings the outside world back in
results.watchOut: Silence reads as absence. Say when you'll be back.
